decision.summary: Do not widen the GC-ISS-0001 pilot to the rest of GC-ISS-* immediately. Keep the representative pilot as a defended verified result and defer broader expansion until a concrete cleanup-value trigger appears.
decision.recommendedNextAction: Hold the result as one verified pilot and leave GC-ISS-0002 through GC-ISS-0005 unchanged for now.
futureReopenTrigger: the contracts root becomes noisy enough that additional ISS redirect relocation produces clear navigation value
a later bounded cleanup round needs one more ISS record moved for consistency or directory reduction
a concrete reader surface starts needing the moved retained bodies rather than simple root-stub landing

whyHold: The pilot already proved the root-stub model in practice, so widening is no longer needed to defend feasibility.
The remaining GC-ISS records still behave as legacy redirects with low current-reader pain; moving them now would produce churn more than new reader value.
Current active issue-governance contracts already read through GC-ICR-0001, GC-ICL-0001, GC-ICT-0001, GC-IID-0001, and GC-IID-0002 rather than through the old GC-ISS root files.
The DOC family is a different current family for doc-first control-plane contracts and is not the semantic owner for these issue-governance records.

docFamily.summary: DOC currently owns doc-first contracts such as role boundaries, source-log compatibility, taxonomy, placement, and family-front-door transition.

gcCurrentRegistry.summary: GC narrow-registry records such as GC-ICR-0001, GC-ICL-0001, GC-ICT-0001, GC-IID-0001, and GC-IID-0002 remain active current governance contracts.

remainingISSDisposition.reason: They are structurally eligible for the same root-stub model, but immediate expansion is not justified until there is concrete cleanup or navigation value beyond what the verified pilot already proved.

prbDisposition.reason: PRB remains outside the ISS pilot lane because its umbrella and sample obligations still require a separate judgment.
